complexes.name: Complex I — NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase
complexes.note: L-shaped proton pump. Electrons: NADH → FMN → 7 on-pathway Fe–S (+ N1a off-path) → Q. Peripheral arm juts ~14 nm into the matrix.

complexes.name: Complex II — Succinate dehydrogenase
complexes.reaction: Succinate + Q → Fumarate + QH₂ · pumps nothing
complexes.note: Citric-acid-cycle enzyme bolted into the membrane. FAD → 3 Fe–S → Q, past heme b (likely ROS guard). Delivers FADH₂ electrons with no proton pumping.

complexes.name: Complex III — Cytochrome bc₁
complexes.reaction: QH₂ + 2 Cyt cₒₓ + 2H⁺ → Q + 2 Cyt cᵣₑ𝒹 + 4H⁺_IMS
complexes.note: The Q-cycle doubles the proton payoff. Rieske Fe–S head physically swings to ferry electrons. Antimycin A kills here.

complexes.name: Complex IV — Cytochrome c oxidase
complexes.note: Where oxygen dies into water. Cyanide/CO block the heme-a₃/CuB binuclear center — the chain backs up instantly.

complexes.name: Complex V — ATP synthase
complexes.subunits: F₀F₁ · α₃β₃ head + γ rotor + c₈-ring
complexes.note: A rotary motor: protons spin the c-ring + γ shaft (up to ~100–150 rev/s), squeezing 3 ATP per turn out of the α₃β₃ head.
